acknowledgements.reverified: THIS FILE'S FIRST RE-PIN SINCE IT WAS ORIGINALLY PINNED, and it is a one-line behavioural change: SHORT_INTEREST_FINANCING_BPS_PER_YEAR moves 0.0 -> 44.7705. default_short_interest_config() already read that constant, so no call site changed; the rest of the diff is the constant's source citation and the module docstring's COSTS section, which asserted the now-false 'financing_bps_per_year stays 0.0'. Verified four ways rather than asserted. (1) THE RATE IS READ FROM THE PERSISTED MEASUREMENT, NOT RETYPED FROM MEMORY: data/research_runs/short_interest_borrow_composition_2026-09-05.json gives composition.si_ratio_hedged_h21.implied_financing_bps_per_year.mean = 44.77049716292157 and measured_financing_bps_per_year.registered_hedged_book = 44.7705, the 4-dp figure that run itself published and fingerprinted; 44.7705 is adopted verbatim. It is the REGISTERED hedged book's rate (short side 89.5410 bp/yr, halved because the config field charges gross notional), NOT the family's long_short rate. (2) THE RESULTING FINGERPRINT WAS PREDICTED BEFORE IT WAS COMPUTED: that report's arms table already recorded d8f3789e2214... for financing 44.7705; config_fingerprint(default_short_interest_config()) now returns d8f3789e22141a4ff8ee1864ec5ae4325393514aa9c8de10f89331f11628d8a6, reproducing it exactly. (3) THE 0.0 BASELINE WAS RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY of the code under test: hashing config_identity's six fields by hand at financing 0.0 reproduces 2dccbf932bfd..., which the 2026-09-05 run read off this registration's live row. (4) BLAST RADIUS WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: all 5 registered families' config_fingerprint and all 58 specs' spec_fingerprint were compared before and after. Exactly two config fingerprints moved (this one and lazy_prices_jaccard_full's, both intended); crypto, quality_cbop and quality_noa_industry_neutral are byte-identical, and ZERO spec fingerprints moved anywhere.
acknowledgements.finding: THIS REGISTRATION WILL PARK AS spec_drift ON ITS NEXT TICK, AND THAT IS THE AUTHORIZED OUTCOME RATHER THAN A REGRESSION. config_fingerprint moves 2dccbf932bfd... -> d8f3789e2214..., detect_config_drift returns a reason, and CrossSectionalForwardValidationRunner._park_as_drifted sets status 'spec_drift', which ACTIVE_STATUSES excludes -- so the row stops ticking and its forward record ends. AUTHORIZED BY THE REPO OWNER IN HIS OWN WORDS, quoted verbatim so the record does not rest on a paraphrase: "รับ borrow rate จริงของ lazy_prices/short_interest_ratio ไหม (จะ auto-park registration) ทำเลย" -- "Adopt the real borrow rate for lazy_prices / short_interest_ratio? (it will auto-park the registration) -- do it." Given in direct response to being told the auto-park consequence, which is therefore authorized, not a side effect. NO STATUS FIELD IS WRITTEN BY THIS CHANGE. The transition is left entirely to the drift gate the runner already runs every tick; no DB row's status was hand-edited, here or anywhere. WHAT IT COSTS: Sharpe +0.4161 -> +0.3233 (-0.0928); DSR 0.7741 -> 0.7308 at N=12, 0.6440 -> 0.6339 at N=481, 0.6261 -> 0.6212 at N=857, on one shared data build; all 12 specs stay positive. Unlike lazy_prices, this spec still clears the 0.50 screening floor at every denominator after paying its own measured rate -- and was and remains far short of the 0.95 validated-edge bar. preservation_score is 0.0 in every arm INCLUDING the untouched baseline (this spec's first-half Sharpe is negative while its second half is strongly positive), so that zero is a property of the strategy and not something the borrow charge did. THE ONE LIMITATION ADOPTION DOES NOT REMOVE, logged rather than buried: financing_bps_per_year is a SCALAR on one config shared by all 12 specs, and the same run measured this family's six long_short specs at 173-215 bp/yr (si_ratio_ls_* sits wholly inside the schedule's expensive tail by construction: tail share exactly 1.0000, book rate exactly 430.00, financing exactly 215.0), so 44.7705 UNDERCHARGES those six by ~4.8x. The constant is set to the REGISTERED book's own rate because that is the book with a live forward record; any reading of a long_short spec's Sharpe or DSR under this config must substitute that report's 215.0 row. This also confirms a prediction this project wrote down and got wrong: the lazy_prices composition report predicted this family's registered rate would be 'far above' lazy_prices'; measured, it is slightly BELOW it (44.7705 vs 48.1644), because the registered spec is the hedged book and not one of the long_short ones that sentence was about. Full record: data/research_runs/borrow_rate_adoption_2026-09-06.txt.
